issues.description: Concept: the shared shelf/stock component used by SealSaloon. The problem statement (UML and text) refers to a class and type named "Stock" and instructs students to use a 'Stock' type for the shared stock attribute (see UML block and the note that 'stock' must be static). However, the provided template and the solution both define and use a class named Inventory that implements the described behavior (Inventory.java). The template also contains an effectively empty Stock.java file (no class defined). This naming mismatch (problem text/UML => 'Stock' vs code => 'Inventory') is likely to confuse students about which class to use and may lead to compile errors if they follow the problem text literally and attempt to reference a 'Stock' class that is not implemented in the template.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the name of the shared inventory type consistent across all artifacts. Two options: (A) Update the problem statement and UML to use 'Inventory' everywhere (and remove the empty Stock.java from the template), or (B) rename the Inventory class/file to Stock (replace Inventory.java with Stock.java or implement Stock.java) and update all references in the template and solution so the class name matches the UML. Also ensure the template does not include an empty Stock.java file (either implement it or delete it) so students do not encounter a missing/empty class.
